name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-19G 'Ghostframe'
description:
The KP-19G is Kang-Petrov's officially sanctioned response to the proliferation of printed and assembled ghost guns in GLMZ—a factory pistol built to the same specifications as the KP-19 but with a deliberately minimal serial number footprint, a frame manufactured from a polymer compound that does not retain chemical fingerprinting agents, and a barrel produced without the standard rifling signature that ballistic forensics rely on. It is, within the letter of GLMZ's weapons registration laws, a legal firearm. The serial number is present and registered. Nothing about it is illegal. Everything about it is designed to be difficult to trace after the fact. Kang-Petrov sells it through select distributors as a 'forensic-reduced platform for sensitive applications,' and the waiting list is always full.

The KP-19G sits in an uncomfortable legal and social space. Arcturus Civil Security has lobbied twice to have it removed from civilian sale and failed both times because Slagworks Industrial—Kang-Petrov's parent corponation—has sufficient leverage in GLMZ's legislative structure to block the classification change. The gun sells primarily to two populations: people with legitimate privacy concerns about ballistic database exposure, and people who intend to use it for things they don't want investigated. The market doesn't distinguish between them, and neither does Kang-Petrov's catalog.

A Ghostframe in hand feels identical to a standard KP-19—same weight, same trigger, same grip texture. The polymer compound has a slightly different visual quality in direct light, a faint translucency that experienced handlers notice. The barrel, rifled in a non-standard pattern that Kang-Petrov refuses to share with ballistics databases, tends to wear faster than the standard version and most owners replace it every 3,000 rounds. Replacement barrels are sold separately, no questions asked.
specifications:
caliber: 9x19mm Standard / 9x19mm Caseless
effective_range: 50m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 17 rounds
weight: 0.75 kg
tactical_use: The KP-19G is operationally identical to the KP-19 in all tactical respects. Its value is entirely post-engagement: a Ghostframe used in an incident produces ballistic evidence that cannot be matched to a specific firearm through standard database queries, and the frame resists chemical fingerprinting that might link it to a specific carrier. Operators who run it accept the faster barrel wear as a cost of doing business. It is not a better gun. It is a harder-to-follow gun.
cultural_context: The Ghostframe is one of the most controversial products in Kang-Petrov's catalog and also one of the most profitable. In fixer circles, carrying one is a professional statement—it says you've thought about consequences. In Arcturus circles, encountering one at a scene is a guaranteed headache. The fact that it's legal makes everyone angrier about it, which seems to be Slagworks Industrial's preferred outcome.
story_hooks: A KP-19G is recovered from a scene where three Zheng-dao Bioelectric researchers were killed. The registration is current, the carrier is registered as a 'privacy consultant,' and the address on file is a mail drop in the South Loop that doesn't exist anymore. Arcturus wants to close the case as unsolvable. Someone else wants it solved badly enough to pay Kyle Corbin-Vasik's full rate.

Kang-Petrov's own head of internal security is found dead with a KP-19G registered to a name that doesn't match any person in GLMZ's population database. The gun's serial number, when traced, leads back to a Slagworks black-budget project that was officially cancelled in 2194.
